t: Donald Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as New White House Chief of Staff
s: US President Donald Trump has announced that immigration hardliner Stephen Miller will succeed Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles, who praised for her outstanding work, is set to transition to the president's political operation. The leadership shake-up comes shortly after the midterm elections, which saw Democrats secure majority control of both the House and Senate. Miller is widely known as a key architect of the administration's mass deportation policies.

t: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production to Focus on Autonomous Vehicles
s: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has confirmed plans to wind down production of the polarizing Cybertruck around mid-2027 at the Texas gigafactory. The futuristic stainless-steel electric pickup faced a troubled journey marked by long delays, numerous recalls, and regulatory hurdles. Tesla now plans to shift its focus toward the production of autonomous Cybercabs, though it remains unclear if manufacturing of the pickup will cease entirely.

t: Meghan Markle's Father Arrested in Florida Over Child Sexual Abuse Material
s: Thomas Markle Snr, the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex, was arrested by federal agents at a nursing home near Tampa, Florida. US prosecutors and the FBI announced that he faces charges related to the possession of child sexual abuse material. The arrest follows an investigation initiated after his son reportedly found suspicious images at his former residence in the Philippines, leading federal agents to seize numerous items from California storage units.

t: Pope Leo XIV Begins Three-Nation South American Tour in Uruguay
s: Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Uruguay, marking the beginning of a three-nation tour across South America that also includes Argentina and Peru. This trip occurs just three weeks after the pontiff underwent lung cancer surgery, which had previously cast doubt on the visit. As a former missionary priest in the region, Pope Leo returns to the continent to engage with local populations in what is considered the most secular country in the region.

t: Bomb Threats Target European Newsrooms and Flights in Coordinated Disruption
s: Multiple newsrooms and numerous flights across Europe faced evacuations and disruptions on Friday following a series of bomb threats. Broadcasters in Ireland, Bulgaria, and the United Kingdom received security alerts from an individual claiming responsibility for the wave of threats. The Irish government described the incidents as most likely a coordinated campaign of disruption targeting the West, while authorities continue to investigate the ongoing security situation.

t: U.S. Judge Temporarily Blocks Construction of Trump's Triumphal Arch
s: A U.S. district judge has temporarily blocked the construction of a planned 250-foot triumphal arch associated with Donald Trump. The project, which received approval from a federal panel, faced opposition from critics who argue the construction is illegal and requires approval from the current Congress. The Trump administration had hoped that work on the large-scale project could begin as early as this week, but the court order has put the plans on hold.

t: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced to 200 Years for Mass Starvation Murders
s: A Kenyan court has sentenced doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison. Mackenzie and his accomplices were convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult. He had ordered his followers to starve themselves and their children to death in a forest so they could meet Jesus.

t: Activists Breach Microsoft Data Center Construction Site Near Amsterdam
s: Protesters breached the construction site of a Microsoft data center near Amsterdam, initiating two days of coordinated global demonstrations. Organized by the 'Stop Dirty Data Centers' coalition with planned actions in 16 countries, the protests highlight growing international backlash against the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. Activists and local communities are increasingly raising concerns over the environmental impact, heavy energy consumption, and strain on power grids caused by the massive data centers required for artificial intelligence.

t: US Economy Exceeds Expectations by Adding 165,000 Jobs in October
s: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, significantly surpassing economists' expectations and lowering the unemployment rate to 4.1%. According to a Labor Department report released on Friday, the job market demonstrated unexpected resilience, outperforming forecasts that had anticipated a much smaller increase in nonfarm payrolls and a steady unemployment rate of 4.2%.

t: Paraguay Faces Political and Financial Crisis Following Ueno Bank Collapse
s: Paraguay is experiencing a severe political and financial crisis following the sudden collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions of customers unable to access their funds. Amid widespread public anger over suspected financial fraud and questions regarding state accountability, lawmakers have resumed impeachment proceedings against President Santiago Peña.

t: Fox Completes $22 Billion Acquisition of Streaming Platform Roku
s: Fox has completed its 22 billion dollar acquisition of the streaming giant Roku. Following a previous investigation by Department of Justice investigators, the finalized transaction significantly expands Fox's digital reach and provides the company with a distinct advantage in the free, ad-supported streaming market.

t: Jay Rockefeller, Former US Senator and West Virginia Governor, Dies at 89
s: John D. "Jay" Rockefeller IV, a scion of a wealthy family and a long-serving Democratic politician, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and spent 30 years in the U.S. Senate, where he was a notable advocate for healthcare, helping expand insurance coverage for low-income children. He passed away at his home in Washington, leaving behind a legacy of public service.

t: Cornell Faculty Senate Passes No-Confidence Vote Over Sexual Assault Handling
s: The Cornell University faculty senate has approved a symbolic resolution declaring no confidence in the central administration and President Michael Kotlikoff. This decision follows deep discontent on campus regarding the university's response to allegations that a former student was gang-raped at a fraternity party in 2024. While the vote is largely symbolic, faculty members hope it will prompt a new approach and leadership.

t: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Faces Growing Impeachment Pressure After Midterms
s: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is facing mounting pressure and potential impeachment calls following a midterm election setback for Republicans. While President Donald Trump has defended him, critics and victorious Democrats are targeting Hegseth in Congress, and some Republicans blame the Iran war he championed for their electoral losses. In response, Hegseth released a social media video vowing to fight the impeachment efforts and defending the military actions.

t: Macklemore Claims Nine U.S. Arenas Refused to Host His 'Free Palestine' Tour
s: Rapper Macklemore has publicly accused nine major U.S. arenas, including Madison Square Garden, of refusing to host his "Free Palestine" fundraising tour. Following successful shows in Europe, the artist took to social media to allege that American venues are employing tactics of intimidation and suppression to block his tour. Macklemore stated that these venues turned down his requests, highlighting the difficulties he has faced in bringing his charitable concert series to the United States.

t: Siberian Tomb Yields Earliest Direct Evidence of Psychoactive Cannabis Use
s: An analysis of hair from a 2,800-year-old Scythian tomb in Siberia has provided researchers with the earliest direct evidence of psychoactive cannabis use. Published in the journal Science, the findings reveal that the ancient culture utilized the plant for its mind-altering effects, shedding new light on the role of cannabis in ancient societies and burial rituals.

t: Netflix Announces Live-Action Stranger Things Prequel Series 'Other Worlds' for 2028
s: Netflix has announced a live-action Stranger Things prequel series titled Other Worlds, set to premiere in 2028. A teaser trailer has been released for the upcoming project. The series takes place in Nevada during the 1950s. Further details about the plot and cast remain limited, but the show is officially scheduled to stream on Netflix in 2028.

t: EU Charges TikTok Over Algorithm and Mental Health Protection Failures
s: The European Commission has charged TikTok with failing to protect users' mental health, stating that its 'For You' page algorithm can lead vulnerable viewers down harmful rabbit holes. Regulators warn that the platform's design risks worsening issues like anxiety and eating disorders. TikTok could face massive fines if it fails to modify its interface and content delivery systems to comply with European Union regulations.

t: Lancet Countdown Report Urges Emergency Response for Climate Health Threats
s: The 2026 Lancet Countdown report highlights that record-breaking climate shocks have created an unprecedented global health emergency, heavily impacting economies and vulnerable populations least responsible for climate change. Marking a decade since its inception and the Paris Agreement, the report stresses that addressing these catastrophic health threats requires a holistic approach and a new long-term emergency response mechanism, as climate change continues to strain global health systems.

t: Wisconsin Reports First Measles Death in Over 35 Years After Infant Dies
s: An infant in southwestern Wisconsin has died from measles, marking the state's first such fatality in over 35 years. Following this tragic event, health experts are set to meet next week to determine whether the United States has lost its official measles elimination status. The incident highlights ongoing public health concerns regarding the preventable viral disease.

t: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production in 2027 to Focus on Cybercab
s: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the company will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas Gigafactory around the middle of 2027. According to Musk, the decision aims to clear factory space to ramp up production of the upcoming Cybercab robotaxi. The planned retirement of the electric pickup truck marks a significant strategic shift for the automaker as it pivots further toward autonomous vehicle manufacturing.

t: Adam Driver Explains Joining Marvel's X-Men Reboot as Mister Sinister
s: Actor Adam Driver has explained why he agreed to star in the upcoming Marvel X-Men reboot as the villain Mister Sinister, after previously turning down multiple MCU offers. Driver stated that it finally felt like the right time, praising the script and the vision for the project. He noted that he was a big fan of X-Men, making this specific opportunity the ideal choice for his entry into the superhero franchise.

t: Former NFL Receiver Antonio Brown Sentenced to Probation in 2025 Shooting Case
s: Former NFL wide receiver Antonio Brown has avoided prison time after pleading guilty to a reduced charge of aggravated assault with a firearm. The case stems from a 2025 shooting incident that occurred outside a celebrity boxing match in Miami. Following his guilty plea, a judge sentenced the former athlete to three years of probation. Brown will not face incarceration for his involvement in the incident, concluding the legal proceedings related to the Miami shooting.

t: Amazon Launches Text-Based Shopping Feature for Alexa AI Assistant
s: Amazon has announced that its AI-powered shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, now supports text-based interactions. US customers can use the feature to search for products, receive recommendations, and make grocery purchases directly via text messages. The company confirmed that this new capability will be rolled out to millions of users over the coming weeks, expanding the functionality of its digital assistant beyond voice commands.

t: Ferrari Boss Vasseur Holds Meeting With Hamilton and Leclerc After Mexico Clash
s: Ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix, Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Frederic Vasseur held a meeting with drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. The discussion followed their first-lap collision at the Mexico Grand Prix. Vasseur emphasized that the team must come first as Ferrari aims to position itself strongly for the world championship next season, addressing potential tensions between the two competitive drivers.

t: US Federal Aviation Administration Begins Historic Upgrade to Ditch Floppy Disks
s: The US Federal Aviation Administration is finally abandoning floppy disks as part of a significant technology upgrade for its information display systems. The agency plans to eliminate floppy disks across 435 sites by the end of 2028. However, officials note that additional funding will be required to complete the broader infrastructure overhaul.

t: Jobe Bellingham receives maiden England call-up alongside brother Jude
s: England head coach Thomas Tuchel has handed Jobe Bellingham his first senior international call-up for the upcoming Nations League fixtures. Jobe joins his older brother, Jude Bellingham, in the squad. Tuchel admitted that Jude had previously urged him to scout the Borussia Dortmund midfielder, though the manager emphasized that Jobe earned his selection entirely on his own merit, creating a unique family opportunity for the siblings.

t: Fly-half Fin Smith fit to start for England against Australia
s: Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening autumn Test against Australia on Sunday. Head coach Steve Borthwick has made four changes to the starting lineup from their July victory over Argentina. Additionally, Ben Curry has been called into the squad to replace his injured twin brother, Tom Curry, ahead of the crucial match.

t: Anthropic IPO Valuation Expectations Drop Following AI Stock Selloff
s: Prospective investors are reconsidering Anthropic's initial public offering valuation, with expectations falling below previous estimates of $1.5 trillion to as low as $1.1 trillion. This shift follows a punishing post-election selloff in artificial intelligence stocks on Wall Street, which has created uncertainty surrounding the upcoming market debut and caused the broader AI trade to sour.

t: The New York Times Reportedly in Talks to Acquire Letterboxd
s: The New York Times Company is reportedly in discussions to acquire Letterboxd, a rapidly growing online platform for film enthusiasts, for approximately $330 million. Letterboxd has experienced significant growth over recent years as a popular digital destination for movie lovers. Representatives for The New York Times Company declined to comment on the ongoing reports regarding the potential multi-million dollar acquisition of the social cataloging service.

t: Democratic Statehouse Wins Set Stage for Clean Energy Policy Shifts
s: Following Tuesday's elections, Democrats erased the Republican Party's advantage in state trifectas, gaining unified control of governorships and legislative chambers. Analysts and advocates report that this shift eliminates previous legislative roadblocks, clearing the path for the enactment of new climate and clean energy policies across multiple states where Republicans previously held the majority of seats and governorships.

t: Voters Decide on Diverse State Ballot Measures During 2026 Midterm Elections
s: During the 2026 midterm elections, voters across the United States cast ballots on a wide range of state policy measures. These initiatives addressed significant issues including environmental protection, abortion rights, transgender youth care, marijuana laws, and science funding. While election outcomes varied by region, the results reflect ongoing national divisions regarding health policy and environmental regulation, with voters in different states delivering distinct verdicts on these critical legislative topics.

t: Lawsuit over similarities between medical dramas The Pitt and ER to proceed
s: A US appeals court has ruled that a lawsuit filed by the widow of ER creator Michael Crichton against the medical drama The Pitt can proceed to a jury trial. The three-judge panel found clear and numerous similarities between the two shows, rejecting an appeal and allowing Sherri Crichton's legal action to move forward toward a trial scheduled for 2027.

t: Novartis Reports Seven Tumor Cases in Children Treated With Zolgensma Gene Therapy
s: Pharmaceutical company Novartis has acknowledged seven previously unknown instances of tumors identified in children who received Zolgensma, a gene therapy designed to treat spinal muscular atrophy. The company is currently investigating these cases to determine if there is a direct link between the medical treatment and the development of the tumors. Novartis disclosed this information following reports of these specific health complications in patients who underwent the therapy.

t: ‘Clicky Ponting’ Amateur Cricketer Banned for Two Years Over Cheating Scandal
s: An amateur English club cricketer known online as 'Clicky Ponting' has received a two-year ban from all cricket after tricking an umpire into believing a batsman had edged the ball by clicking his fingers while fielding. Following the online notoriety of the incident from July, his team, Saltburn CC’s second XI, was relegated, and the club faced a fine imposed by the league.

t: Channel 4 Axes Married at First Sight UK Following Rape Allegations
s: Channel 4 has cancelled the reality show Married at First Sight UK following two independent reviews triggered by allegations of rape and sexual misconduct by female participants during production. The broadcaster stated it will reallocate the show's budget to distinctive new programming and issued another apology to the women involved in the incidents. The decision marks the end of the popular series after the serious safety and conduct concerns came to light.

t: NASA Unveils X-70 Fractal Experimental Aircraft for Advanced Aviation Research
s: NASA has officially unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Designed as a high-performance, adaptable research platform, the crewed aircraft features rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology to accelerate the testing of advanced aviation systems. This initiative is part of the agency's broader effort to expand its fleet of X-planes. The X-70 Fractal is currently scheduled to conduct its first test flight within the next two years.

t: Apple Announces Over 100,000 Optimized Apps Available for iPhone Duo
s: Two weeks after the official launch of the iPhone Duo, Apple has announced that the App Store features over 100,000 apps specifically built and optimized for the foldable device. Susan Prescott, Apple's VP of Worldwide Developer Relations, expressed gratitude for the developers' quick adoption and creativity, noting that thousands of additional optimized applications continue to arrive on the platform daily as developer support for the new hardware expands rapidly.

t: British Doctor Evacuated from DR Congo to London for Ebola Treatment
s: A British doctor who tested positive for Ebola while working in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been medically evacuated to the United Kingdom. The patient is currently receiving specialist care in a high-level isolation unit at the Royal Free Hospital in London. The UK government confirmed the evacuation on Thursday, emphasizing that the risk to the general public remains low as the doctor undergoes treatment for the virus.

t: Earth's Churning Mantle Linked to Great Unconformity Origins
s: Recent scientific studies suggest that continental-scale uplift and subsidence, driven by mantle convection and dynamic topography, played a key role in creating and preserving the Great Unconformity. This geological phenomenon is characterized by Cambrian deposits resting directly on much older rocks, a mystery that researchers have long sought to explain.

t: Meta Introduces Spaces for Collaborative Work With Muse AI
s: Meta has announced Spaces, a new feature allowing users to build customized, app-like experiences within its Muse AI agent. The update enables the AI assistant to create interactive environments such as shopping hubs, school dashboards, music trackers, and trivia games directly inside the Muse application, offering a novel way for users to collaborate and interact with their AI helpers.

t: Lando Norris Tops Sao Paulo Grand Prix First Practice Ahead of Kimi Antonelli
s: McLaren driver Lando Norris set the fastest time during the first practice session at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Friday. Newly crowned Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli finished second fastest in his first track session since securing the title in Mexico the previous weekend.

t: Global Fund Appoints Mark Dybul as New Head Amid Financial and Political Challenges
s: Mark Dybul has been appointed to lead the Global Fund once again, returning to the organization with the goal of helping countries control HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria. Health leaders have welcomed his appointment amidst a rapidly changing global health landscape, even as the organization faces significant financial and political challenges in its mission.

t: US-Funded Baby Vaccine Trial in Guinea-Bissau Cancelled Amid Ethical Concerns
s: A US-funded vaccine trial involving babies in Guinea-Bissau was cancelled after being condemned as unethical and neocolonial because half of the participating infants would not receive the vaccine. Meanwhile, a separate clinical trial called the Tumaini trial has begun to find effective vaccines against the Bundibugyo virus, an infection that has caused over 5,000 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

t: Dallas Wings Teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd Confirm Past Relationship Split
s: Dallas Wings backcourt teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd have confirmed on a podcast that they ended their romantic relationship more than a year ago. During the discussion, the duo dismissed speculation that their personal relationship influenced the WNBA draft and condemned the hostile messages directed at their friends and family. They also talked about the team's season and Fudd's ongoing recovery from knee surgery.

t: Bryson DeChambeau Faces DP World Tour Deadline Amid LIV Golf Uncertainty
s: Golfer Bryson DeChambeau faces a November 15 deadline to state his intention to become a DP World Tour member in 2027 or risk missing out. This development comes as reports about LIV Golf potentially shuttering raise significant questions regarding the future paths for some of the world's top professional golfers.

t: NWSL Playoffs Begin With Analysts Evaluating Contenders and Championship Prospects
s: As the National Women's Soccer League playoffs arrive, sports analysts and panels are breaking down the strengths, star players, squad depth, and potential flaws of every contending team. Discussions focus on top candidates reaching the championship game in Washington, D.C., potential dark horses, and the key storylines that shaped the league during a competitive sports season.

t: Singapore Airlines Unveils S$2 Billion Cabin Upgrade Featuring Sky's Largest Double Bed
s: Singapore Airlines has announced a S$2 billion cabin upgrade for its long-haul flights, featuring what it claims is the largest double bed in commercial aviation. Set to launch next year, the extensive makeover includes new first-class and business-class cabins designed to offer enhanced privacy, space, and luxury. This initiative highlights the intense competition among global airlines to attract wealthy travelers seeking premium in-flight experiences.

t: Danny McBride and Bradley Cooper's 'G.I. Joe' Movie Set for 2028
s: Paramount has announced that the upcoming reimagining of the 'G.I. Joe' franchise, directed by Danny McBride and starring Bradley Cooper as Duke, will receive a wide theatrical release on October 20, 2028. McBride co-wrote the screenplay with Jeff Fradley and John Carcieri based on the Hasbro toy line and comic book origins. Plot details for the new film are currently being kept under tight security.

t: Hunger Games Prequel Surpasses Wicked in Strong Box Office Presales
s: Lionsgate’s upcoming film 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' is demonstrating strong performance with box office presales surpassing those of Universal’s 'Wicked'. Advance ticket sales have set a new post-COVID record for Lionsgate, positioning the movie for a projected opening floor of over 80 million dollars.

t: Google criticized for conditioning school search access on mandatory AI integration
s: Google is facing criticism for requiring educational institutions to accept its artificial intelligence features in order to access its search engine, even in districts where AI use is currently prohibited. Critics argue that the technology company should not dictate education policy, noting that the policy deprives schools of meaningful choices regarding technology adoption in the classroom.

t: Sophisticated Fake Job Interview Scams Target Job Seekers and Companies
s: Recent reports highlight the growing sophistication of fake job interview scams, which have impacted major companies like Binance and caused significant financial losses. While poor legitimate interviews offer workplace lessons, fraudulent recruitment processes present severe security risks. Experts advise job seekers to remain vigilant and watch for new warning signs to avoid falling victim to these elaborate employment scams during their search.

t: Blizzard Entertainment Launches New World of Warcraft: Forever Game Mode
s: Blizzard Entertainment has officially released World of Warcraft: Forever, a new game mode that transports players into an alternate reality version of the long-running online title. Following a successful launch earlier this week, the developer addressed questions regarding the timing of the release. Blizzard explained the specific factors that led to the decision to finally introduce this Classic+ style experience, which has already garnered significant attention from the gaming community.

t: NASA's Swift Telescope Plunges to Earth as Hubble Faces Similar Fate
s: NASA's Swift space telescope has plunged back to Earth and disintegrated upon re-entry after operating for more than twenty years, following a failed attempt to raise its decaying orbit. Meanwhile, the Hubble Space Telescope is also gradually losing altitude and faces a potential fiery re-entry around 2032. NASA is currently seeking proposals from the private sector to explore potential methods for saving and maintaining Hubble's operations.

t: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Summoned by US Congress Over Chinese Espionage Concerns
s: US lawmakers have summoned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to appear before Congress to address questions regarding his ties to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Members of Congress are seeking answers about the potential national security implications and relationships involving the tech executive, following growing concerns related to Chinese espionage activities. The inquiry focuses specifically on the nature of these connections and what the company knows about the situation.

t: Remembering "Star Trek" Actor Patrick Stewart
s: Actor Patrick Stewart, renowned for his work with the Royal Shakespeare Company and as Captain Picard in "Star Trek," passed away on October 28. In a special broadcast tribute, critic David Bianculli reflects on the acclaimed performer's remarkable career. Additionally, a rebroadcast of a 2020 interview allows audiences to remember Stewart in his own words, celebrating his lasting and influential legacy across both classical theatre and science fiction television.

t: UK employers to be legally required to publish salaries in job adverts
s: Employers in the United Kingdom will be legally required to publish salary details on all new job advertisements. Announced by Andy Burnham, the new measure aims to empower jobseekers, help them know what a job pays before applying, and prevent potential pay discrimination. Workers' rights campaigners note the change will especially assist young people and women in achieving more equal pay. The government describes the policy as part of ongoing efforts to improve people's lives.

t: Airbnb Announces Plans to Launch AI Travel Agent in Early 2027
s: Airbnb has officially announced plans to introduce an AI-powered travel agent during the first half of 2027. Revealed in the company's Q3 2026 shareholder letter, the tool is designed to assist users with comprehensive trip planning, comparing travel options, managing bookings, and providing support throughout their stay. While current AI agents handle routine tasks, Airbnb aims for this new system to manage complex travel arrangements, marking a significant expansion of the platform's digital service capabilities.

t: Mild UK Autumn Triggers Premature Tree Flowering, Worrying Experts
s: Mild autumn temperatures across the UK have caused trees to experience a premature spring, leading to early flowering following the ninth consecutive month of above-average temperatures. Experts warn that this disruption could cause long-term harm to pollinators and local ecosystems.

t: Experts Address Social Media Claims Linking Facial Features to Iron Deficiency
s: Social media users are increasingly claiming that specific facial features, such as dark circles or dry skin, indicate iron deficiency, a phenomenon dubbed 'ferritin face.' However, experts like Professor Hal Drakesmith of Oxford University clarify that these visual signs are not reliable diagnostic tools. While iron deficiency is a common health issue, medical professionals emphasize that accurate diagnosis requires proper testing rather than relying on subjective observations or online trends.

t: Canadian Politician Petitions Government to Help BioWare Leave EA
s: A Canadian politician has initiated an official government petition aimed at helping the video game developer BioWare separate from its parent company, Electronic Arts (EA). BioWare, widely known for developing major franchises such as Mass Effect, operates as a subsidiary of EA. The petition calls for government intervention or support to facilitate the studio's independence, though specific details regarding the mechanics of such a buyout remain tied to the political appeal.

t: China Reports 3.1% Decline in Quarterly CO2 Emissions
s: China experienced a 3.1% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions during the third quarter of 2026. According to analysis by Carbon Brief, this represents the most significant quarterly decline in the country's emissions since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic. The decrease occurred amidst the ongoing Hormuz crisis, which has impacted global energy dynamics. This data highlights a notable shift in China's recent emissions trajectory, marking a departure from previous trends observed in recent years.

t: Rapidly Developing Super El Niño on Track to Peak in December
s: A rapidly developing super El Niño is currently on track to peak at the end of the year in December. According to reports, this ongoing meteorological phenomenon is likely to push average global temperatures significantly higher as it reaches its maximum strength. Scientists and analysts describe the intensity of the event as simply staggering, highlighting its potential impact on global climate patterns.

t: Min Jin Lee Announces New Novel 'American Hagwon' Focusing on Education
s: Author Min Jin Lee has discussed her upcoming novel, 'American Hagwon,' the third installment in her diaspora quartet following 'Pachinko.' The book explores the promise and perils of Western education for a Korean family willing to sacrifice everything for their children's academic success. The story centers on private after-school academies known as hagwons, where parents invest heavily to turbocharge their children's performance, reflecting the author's meticulous decade-long writing process.

t: Cop31 Climate Summit to Highlight Global Fossil Fuel Contradictions in Turkey
s: The upcoming Cop31 climate summit, set to begin next week in Turkey, will focus heavily on the global transition to clean electricity. Observers note that holding the major climate conference under the presidency of a country heavily reliant on coal underscores the ongoing conflicts and contradictions inherent in the world's continued dependence on fossil fuels.

t: Iowa Residents Oppose Proposed Natural Gas Plant Amid Data Center Growth
s: Nearly 50 residents gathered in Fairfax, Iowa, to voice their opposition to a proposed natural gas plant located less than three miles from the town. Prompted to share their emotions at the meeting, attendees used their phones to submit words such as angry, disgusted, and scared. The facility is being considered as data centers increasingly move into the area, raising environmental and community concerns among local populations who feel anxious about the industrial development.

t: Parkinson’s Disease Linked to Vicious Cycle of Brain Waste Drainage Disruption
s: New research suggests that Parkinson’s disease may be driven by a self-reinforcing cycle involving toxic protein clumps and impaired brain waste removal systems. Scientists believe these two factors feed off each other, creating a vicious cycle that accelerates the progression of the condition. Understanding this mechanism could provide new insights into how the disease develops and potentially lead to future therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring proper waste drainage in the brain.

t: U.S. Midterm Voters Approve New Restrictions on Data Center Development
s: Following the U.S. midterm elections, the artificial intelligence and tech industry faces potential regulatory challenges after voters approved numerous ballot measures. Across 41 data center-related measures voted on Tuesday, the vast majority resulted in decisions to impose stricter regulations on data center development. These outcomes reflect growing public scrutiny and could significantly impact the future expansion of infrastructure supporting the technology sector.

t: Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble Canceled Less Than a Year After Launch
s: Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, a mobile spin-off of the flagship PlayStation franchise, has been canceled less than a year after its initial announcement and launch. The news marks a swift end for the mobile title, which expanded the popular video game series into the mobile gaming market before its sudden termination.

t: Record-Breaking Fast-Spinning Magnet Could Help Uncover New Physics
s: Researchers have developed a magnet barely wider than a human hair that ranks among the fastest-spinning objects ever created. This microscopic device could serve as a valuable tool for fundamental physics experiments and various applications in quantum technology, according to recent reports.

t: NASA Prepares Cave-Hunting Robot GIMLI for Future Moon Base Exploration
s: As preparations for establishing a future moon base accelerate, NASA is developing a cave-hunting robot named GIMLI. According to reports, this specialized robotic explorer is designed to scout lunar caves ahead of human astronauts, playing a crucial role in the upcoming exploration and utilization of the moon.

t: Global Tech Stocks Plunge Amid Fears of AI Slowdown After US Midterms
s: Global financial markets experienced significant volatility as major tech stocks, including Apple, Tesla, and Nvidia, lost approximately one trillion dollars in a single trading session. The sharp decline on Wall Street followed the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, fueling investor anxiety over potential artificial intelligence regulation and a broader slowdown in the tech sector. This drop highlights mounting concerns that the current artificial intelligence boom may be facing a market correction.

t: Unexpected Feedback Loop May Drive Extreme Heatwaves, Study Suggests
s: Research indicates that a combination of dry soil and high pressure creates an unexpected feedback loop, amplifying extreme heat. This mechanism helps explain why regions such as Europe are experiencing record-breaking heatwaves much earlier than what current climate models had predicted, highlighting a gap in our understanding of rapid temperature surges.

t: Jim Cramer Shares Stock Updates and 2027 Outlook at Annual Meeting
s: During the Investing Club's fourth annual meeting, Jim Cramer provided updates on various club stocks, revealed a new stock to buy, and discussed his outlook for the year 2027. He also answered questions from both the live audience and members participating from home during the broadcast.

t: Nvidia Hardware Worth $11.4 Million Disappears En Route to Texas
s: Six pallets of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million vanished while being transported from Oakland to Texas. Two months after the incident occurred, law enforcement has made no arrests in connection with the missing shipment, and the investigation remains ongoing.

t: Hundreds of Exposed Artex AI Hacking Tools Found Online
s: Security researchers discovered hundreds of servers hosting the Artex penetration testing tool publicly exposed to the internet. This exposure allows unauthorized individuals open access to the sensitive hacking tools, raising significant security concerns regarding how these servers were configured and maintained.

t: Short Bursts of Vigorous Daily Exercise May Reduce Dementia Risk
s: New research suggests that engaging in less than four minutes of vigorous physical activity daily may significantly lower the risk of developing dementia. Activities such as carrying heavy groceries or rushing to catch a bus provide the necessary intensity to benefit brain health. These brief, incidental bursts of exercise appear to have a measurable positive impact on cognitive longevity, offering a simple and accessible strategy for maintaining long-term neurological well-being.

t: China Nominates Dr. Song Li for World Health Organization Director-General Position
s: China has officially nominated Dr. Song Li as a candidate for the Director-General position at the World Health Organization. This unexpected move is viewed by analysts as a strategic effort by Beijing to increase its influence in global health governance. The nomination reflects China's broader ambition to assert leadership in international institutions, particularly as the nation seeks to play a more prominent role in multilateral organizations following shifts in global political dynamics.

t: India to Cap Prices on 137 Cancer Drugs Following Court Ruling
s: Following a Supreme Court ruling, India's National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority is set to limit trade margins on 137 life-saving cancer drugs. This regulatory move aims to make oncology treatments more affordable for patients across the country. The decision addresses concerns over the high cost of essential medications, ensuring stricter price controls within the pharmaceutical market as reported from Mumbai.

t: Malaysian Leader Jemilah Mahmood's Impact on Planetary Health Highlighted
s: In the year 2000, Malaysian obstetrician and gynaecologist Professor Jemilah Mahmood was deeply moved by television images of devastating floods in Mozambique, specifically a rescue of a woman giving birth in a tree. Nearly two decades later, in 2019, while visiting clinics established following those floods, a local midwife introduced her to a young adult whose mother had been rescued from the tree during the disaster.

t: Physician's New Book Examines High-Risk Pregnancies Following the Dobbs Decision
s: In his book Impossible Choices, physician David N Hackney describes how he and his colleagues were unprepared for the US Supreme Court's Dobbs v Jackson Women's Health Organization decision on June 24, 2022. The ruling eliminated the constitutional right to abortion, resulting in a near-total abortion ban within hours and raising critical questions about medical care for high-risk pregnancies.

t: Global Tobacco Mortality Projected at One Billion in the 21st Century
s: Despite a decline in adult smoking rates across numerous high-income nations, the global death toll attributed to tobacco is projected to reach one billion lives during the twenty-first century. Experts emphasize that this ongoing crisis remains an entirely preventable pandemic, highlighting the persistent and massive public health challenge posed by tobacco exposure worldwide.

t: Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group Arrives in Singapore
s: The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group arrived in Singapore on Friday for a scheduled port visit. The group includes the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt, cruiser USS Chosin, and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton and USS Decatur. Following this stop, the strike group is expected to deploy to the Middle East.

t: French Sailors Conduct Close-in Defense Drills Aboard BRF Resupply Ship
s: French sailors aboard the Bâtiment ravitailleur de forces-class resupply ship FS Jacques Stosskopf recently conducted a close-in defense drill at the Toulon naval base. Wearing protective gear including gloves and flash hoods, the crew prepared for close-range security operations. The modern logistics vessel, one of Europe's most advanced combat supply ships, was berthed alongside anti-aircraft assets during the training exercise at its home port in southern France.

t: Artificial Intelligence Emerges as a New Dealbreaker on Dating Apps
s: As people increasingly use dating platforms to meet new individuals and explore new cities, artificial intelligence is becoming a notable factor in romantic connections. Users swiping through profiles on applications like Hinge are encountering AI-related prompts and trends, reflecting how modern technology increasingly influences contemporary dating dynamics and personal preferences among young urban professionals.

t: Fiona Apple and the Bolt Cutters Cover Mother Earth’s Song
s: Fiona Apple and the Bolt Cutters have recorded a cover of Mother Earth’s song "Revolution." The track was featured on the compilation album Right Now, which raises funds to benefit Doctors Without Borders. The project brings together various artists to support the international medical humanitarian organization's critical efforts worldwide.

t: Independent Films 'I Play Rocky' and Others Debut in Stacked Weekend
s: A variety of independent films, including 'I Play Rocky', 'Club Kid', and 'Wild Horse Nine', are launching in theaters during a busy specialty box office weekend. Screen counts for these new releases and continuing award contenders range from single locations to wide distributions. Meanwhile, Netflix's 'La Bola Negra' is expanding its theatrical reach to its widest release yet, highlighting a diverse lineup for moviegoers.

t: Sony Pictures Acquires Rights to Liv Zander’s ‘The Heartstring Duet’
s: Sony Pictures has acquired the film adaptation rights to Liv Zander’s bestselling dark fantasy romance book series, The Heartstring Duet. Comprising the novels Crown Me Dead and Crown Me Yours, the self-published series gained viral popularity through its unique blend of dark fantasy, horror, and romance elements. The project is currently set to be developed as a feature film by the studio, bringing the popular literary property to the big screen.

t: Simon Pegg Joins Paul Giamatti in Horror Film 'Boutique'
s: BAFTA winner Simon Pegg has joined two-time Oscar nominee Paul Giamatti in the upcoming horror film 'Boutique'. The story follows an American tourist, played by Giamatti, who visits an eerie English seaside town that inspired his favorite reclusive author, portrayed by Pegg. There, the tourist becomes entangled with a murderous plot. Manifest is handling international sales for the project at the American Film Market.

t: US Stock Futures Decline Following Market Correction and Worst Session Since April
s: US stock futures declined following a significant market sell-off on Thursday. The Nasdaq index entered correction territory, contributing to the worst session for all three major averages since April 2025. Investors are now closely monitoring upcoming payroll data for further economic signals. This downturn reflects heightened market volatility as traders react to recent economic developments and await critical labor market reports to gauge the future direction of the economy.

t: Saudi National Pleads Not Guilty to Planting Recording Device at OpenAI
s: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national, has pleaded not guilty to charges of planting a recording device inside a conference room at the artificial intelligence company OpenAI. The suspect faces legal proceedings regarding the alleged espionage incident within the prominent tech firm. Authorities continue to handle the case as the investigation unfolds based on the initial charges brought against him.

t: Tech Stocks Face Continued Market Volatility in the Week Ahead
s: Investors are concluding a turbulent week in the financial markets, with analysts anticipating that the current instability will persist. As the market prepares for the week ahead, attention remains focused on the technology sector, which continues to experience significant fluctuations. Market participants are closely monitoring upcoming developments, as experts suggest that the recent volatility affecting tech stocks is unlikely to subside immediately, potentially leading to further uncertainty for traders in the coming days.

t: US Army Renames Culinary Specialists to Tactical Field Feeding Specialists
s: The US Army has officially changed the job title for soldiers with the 92G occupation identifier. Previously known as culinary specialists, these personnel will now be referred to as tactical field feeding specialists. This update modernizes the title to better reflect the operational nature of their duties in supporting military personnel across various field environments, ensuring clarity in their specialized military role.

t: Edmund Richardson Wins Baillie Gifford Prize for Alexander the Great Biography
s: Edmund Richardson has won the £50,000 Baillie Gifford prize for his acclaimed biography of Alexander the Great, titled 'Alexander: God, King, Man'. The book details the life of the ancient ruler, who became king of Macedon at age 20 following his father's assassination in 336 BC. Reviewers praised the work as a dazzling adventure and a riveting piece of history that connects ancient events to the modern world, highlighting the author's extensive research.

t: Billions of Gallons of Raw Sewage Pour Into Chicago River After Storms
s: Following heavy rainfall in early October, billions of gallons of raw sewage have poured into the Chicago River and surrounding waterways. Workers and residents near the affected areas have reported visible floating sewage and strong odors after the severe storms. The overflow highlights ongoing concerns regarding the region's stormwater management and infrastructure capacity during extreme weather events.

t: US and Colombian Troops Launch Military Exercise Amid Strategic Pivot
s: Hundreds of American and Colombian troops have begun a large-scale military exercise in Colombia. This joint operation coincides with the Pentagon increasing its strategic focus on the Western Hemisphere, marking a notable shift in military priorities and bilateral cooperation in the region.

t: U.S. Military Extends Okinawa Curfew and Alcohol Restrictions for Junior Marines
s: The U.S. military has extended a 30-day curfew and continued alcohol restrictions for junior service members in Okinawa, following a murder indictment. The III Marine Expeditionary Force announced that personnel in pay grades E-1 through E-4 must remain in their personal housing between 12 a.m. and 5 a.m. This measure extends the previous restrictions that were originally scheduled to expire on Sunday.

t: Breaking Defense Releases Free AUSA 2026 After-Action Report eBook
s: Defense publication Breaking Defense has released a free after-action report eBook covering the AUSA 2026 conference. The publication highlights the event's biggest stories, key U.S. Army priorities, and major industry developments. The report is available for download without requiring user registration.

t: DoD Awards Viasat $450 Million Contract for Golden Dome Satellite Network
s: The United States Department of Defense has selected Viasat to design, field, and scale a mission operation center for the Space Data Network Backbone. This indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract carries a maximum value of $450 million. The new operations center will support data relay for the Golden Dome satellite network, enhancing military space operations and communication capabilities through advanced infrastructure development.

t: Yemeni Forces and Houthis Trade Blame for Deadly Taiz Market Strikes
s: Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels have traded blame following a deadly strike on the al-Hadara market in the al-Waziiya district of Taiz governorate. According to Houthi rebels, the attack resulted in the deaths of at least 30 people. Both sides deny responsibility for the violence, which has added to the ongoing civilian toll in the war-torn region.

t: Europe's combat aircraft strategy shifts amid new fighter programs and drone integration
s: Europe's future combat aircraft strategy is undergoing significant changes, influenced by Germany's upcoming strategic decisions, the evolving status of the Global Combat Air Programme, and the increasing integration of collaborative combat aircraft. These developments are collectively reshaping how the continent plans its military aviation capabilities, moving away from original blueprints as new technological and geopolitical factors emerge.

t: Trevor Nunn Directs New Play 'Speculations' Featuring Dorothy Kilgallen and Marilyn Monroe
s: Director Trevor Nunn has debuted 'Speculations,' a new play written by Torben Betts, at the Marylebone Theatre in London. The production explores the life and conspiracy theories of real-life American journalist Dorothy Kilgallen, portrayed by Janie Dee. The narrative centers on Kilgallen's investigations into the Kennedy family and features a dramatic portrayal of Marilyn Monroe, examining the intersection of celebrity culture and political intrigue within the mid-20th century American landscape.

t: RuPaul's Drag Race UK Crowns Winner as BBC Axes Series
s: The United Kingdom spin-off of the global reality television hit RuPaul's Drag Race has crowned its latest winner. However, the announcement coincides with the decision by the BBC to shelve the popular series after completing eight seasons on the network.

t: Juneau, Alaska, Relies on Imports and Community Sharing for Food Security
s: Juneau, Alaska, faces significant challenges in food production due to limited arable land and a short growing season. Because the city is geographically isolated, with roads ending abruptly outside the capital, residents rely heavily on food transported by air or water. To supplement these supplies, the community maintains deep-rooted traditions of sharing resources, ensuring that residents and the land continue to support one another despite the harsh environmental conditions.

t: Spice Girls Release Singles Collection Box Set Amid Ongoing Reunion Teasers
s: The Spice Girls have released a new singles collection box set through Virgin. While fans continue to endure frequent tabloid reports and hints from band member Mel B regarding a potential full reunion, film, or documentary, the new box set has been described by reviewers as a commercial release that offers little new material, aside from a curio track featuring Posh Spice on lead vocals.

t: Australia Faces Criticism Over New Coal and Gas Project Approvals Ahead of COP31
s: The Australian government is facing growing scrutiny regarding its recent approvals of coal and gas projects. Critics argue these decisions contradict climate commitments, particularly as the nation prepares for the upcoming COP31 climate summit. Concerns have been raised about the environmental impact of these fossil fuel developments and the potential implications for Australia's international climate reputation, with observers questioning the consistency of the government's climate policy in the lead-up to the global conference.

t: Wynonna Judd Discusses Family Tragedy and Raw New Album
s: Country star Wynonna Judd has released a raw, pared-back new album that reflects on the death of her mother and decades of personal struggles. Abandoning Nashville slickness, the singer describes the project as a labor of love born from navigating deep personal pain and family tragedy.

t: BBC Radio 1Xtra Launches First-Ever Official UK Rap Chart
s: BBC Radio 1Xtra has launched the UK's first-ever official rap chart, dedicated to celebrating the top 20 best-selling UK rap tracks each week. Hosted by DJ Kenny Allstar, the new weekly broadcast aims to provide a dedicated platform highlighting the success and popularity of rap music across the country, establishing a recognized standard for the genre.

t: Week in Wildlife: Highlights from Global Nature Photography
s: A selection of this week's best wildlife photographs from around the world captures various animals in their natural habitats, including an autumnal deer, golden jackals, and an oily-kneed beetle. These striking images highlight the beauty and diversity of global fauna, showcasing captivating moments of wildlife behavior and seasonal changes as documented by photographers globally.

t: Distinguishing Bank Voles and Wood Mice in Clophill Lakes Footage Proves Challenging
s: At the Clophill Lakes nature reserve in Bedfordshire, a wildlife observer reviewing a series of nine-second video clips encountered difficulty distinguishing between bank voles and wood mice. Analyzing the footage to count the number of bank voles appearing in the recordings proved challenging because the two small mammal species appear very similar on the short videos, leading to uncertainty in identifying the animals correctly.
